title: استخرهای ارزش Zcash
description: Zcash وجوه را در سیستم‌های حسابداری مجزایی به نام استخرهای ارزش جدا می‌کند. هر استخر قواعد رمزنگاری و ویژگی‌های حریم خصوصی خاص خود را دارد، در حالی که پروتکل…
text: استخرهای ارزش Zcash خلاصه Zcash در حال حاضر 5 استخر ارزش دارد: Sprout (قدیمی)، Sapling، Orchard (فقط خرج‌کردنی)، Ironwood و شفاف. Ironwood استخر محافظت‌شدهٔ اصلی فعلی است و از زمان ارتقای NU6.3 در 28 جولای 2026 فعال است. Orchard اکنون فقط خرج‌کردنی است: هیچ ارزش جدیدی نمی‌تواند وارد آن شود و وجوه موجود از آن به Ironwood مهاجرت می‌کنند. Sapling (آدرس‌های z که با zs شروع می‌شوند) همچنان به‌طور گسترده پشتیبانی می‌شود و همچنان مقدار قابل‌توجهی ZEC محافظت‌شده را ایمن نگه می‌دارد. آدرس‌های شفاف (t...) هیچ حریم خصوصی‌ای برای تراکنش فراهم نمی‌کنند و مشابه Bitcoin عمل می‌کنند. Sprout یک استخر محافظت‌شدهٔ قدیمی است که از استفادهٔ فعال کنار گذاشته شده است. مهاجرت از Orchard به Ironwood در حال انجام است و توسط دروازه به‌صورت عمومی حسابرسی می‌شود. برای قوی‌ترین تضمین‌های حریم خصوصی، کاربران باید همچنان هر زمان که ممکن است تراکنش‌های محافظت‌شده به محافظت‌شده (z → z) را ترجیح دهند. آشنایی با استخرهای ارزش Zcash Zcash وجوه را در سیستم‌های حسابداری مجزایی به نام استخرهای ارزش جدا می‌کند. هر استخر قواعد رمزنگاری و ویژگی‌های حریم خصوصی خاص خود را دارد، در حالی که پروتکل کل ارزشی را که میان آن‌ها جابه‌جا می‌شود ردیابی می‌کند. امروزه شبکه شامل پنج استخر ارزش اصلی است: شفاف — عمومی و کاملاً قابل مشاهده به‌صورت on-chain. Sapling — نخستین استخر محافظت‌شدهٔ مدرن که به‌طور گسترده پذیرفته شد و همچنان فعال است. Orchard — استخر محافظت‌شدهٔ اصلی پیشین که اکنون فقط خرج‌کردنی است. Ironwood — استخر محافظت‌شدهٔ اصلی فعلی که با NU6.3 معرفی شد. Sprout — استخر محافظت‌شدهٔ اولیه که در سال 2016 همراه با Zcash راه‌اندازی شد. با تکامل Zcash، ممکن است استخرهای محافظت‌شدهٔ جدیدی برای بهبود امنیت، حریم خصوصی، کاربردپذیری و قابلیت حسابرسی معرفی شوند، در حالی که سازگاری با وجوه موجود حفظ می‌شود. شکل 1: نموداری که سه استخر محافظت‌شده (Sprout، Sapling و Orchard) را تا 29 اکتبر 2025، پیش از فعال شدن Ironwood، نشان می‌دهد استخرهای محافظت‌شده استخر Ironwood Ironwood استخر محافظت‌شدهٔ اصلی فعلی است. این استخر در 28 جولای 2026 در بلوک 3,428,143 به‌عنوان بخشی از ارتقای شبکه NU6.3 فعال شد و ارزش محافظت‌شدهٔ جدید اکنون در آن قرار می‌گیرد. دلیل وجود آن این است که در ماه می 2026 آسیب‌پذیری‌ای در سیستم اثبات Orchard پیدا شد. هیچ شواهدی وجود ندارد که این آسیب‌پذیری هرگز مورد سوءاستفاده قرار گرفته باشد، اما این نقص به این معنا بود که سالم بودن عرضهٔ محافظت‌شده را نمی‌شد تنها با اثبات‌ها اثبات کرد. شبکه به‌جای وصله کردن در همان جا، استخر تازه‌ای با مداری اصلاح‌شده ایجاد کرد و ارزش را از طریق دروازه‌ای منتقل کرد که هر سکه را به‌صورت عمومی می‌شمارد. همین حسابداری است که این تضمین را بازمی‌گرداند که عرضهٔ محافظت‌شده به‌طور کامل پشتوانه دارد. Ironwood از مدل Action و اثبات‌های Halo 2 در Orchard دوباره استفاده می‌کند، بنابراین در استفادهٔ روزمره به همان شکل رفتار می‌کند. دو چیز جدید است: تراکنش‌ها از قالب v6 استفاده می‌کنند و note‌های Ironwood تحت ZIP 2005 قابل بازیابی در برابر کوانتوم هستند، به این معنا که اگر یک رایانهٔ کوانتومی در آینده رمزنگاری امروزی را بشکند، سابقهٔ on-chain یک سکه قابل بازیابی باقی می‌ماند. این یک مسیر بازیابی است، نه مقاومت در برابر کوانتوم، و برای استخرهای قدیمی‌تر کاربرد ندارد. شما به آدرس جدیدی نیاز ندارید. آدرس‌های یکپارچه چندین گیرنده را در خود جای می‌دهند و کیف‌پول‌ها استخر مناسب را برای شما انتخاب می‌کنند. استخر Orchard شکل 2: نموداری که استخر Orchard را تا 29 اکتبر 2025، پیش از فعال شدن Ironwood، نشان می‌دهد استخر محافظت‌شدهٔ Orchard در 31 می 2022 به‌عنوان بخشی از ارتقای شبکه NU5 فعال شد. Orchard پروتکل محافظت‌شدهٔ جدیدی را معرفی کرد که نیاز به تنظیمات اولیه مورد اعتماد را از میان برداشت و به استخر محافظت‌شدهٔ اصلی مورد استفادهٔ آدرس‌های یکپارچه (UA) تبدیل شد. Orchard با کاهش نشت فراداده‌های تراکنش و معرفی مدل تراکنش انعطاف‌پذیرتری مبتنی بر Actionها به‌جای ورودی‌ها و خروجی‌های محافظت‌شدهٔ سنتی، کاربردپذیری، کارایی و حریم خصوصی را به‌طور چشمگیری بهبود داد. از زمان فعال شدن ارتقای Ironwood در 28 جولای 2026، Orchard فقط خرج‌کردنی است. هیچ ارزش جدیدی نمی‌تواند وارد این استخر شود. وجوهی که از قبل در آن نگهداری می‌شوند همچنان قابل خرج کردن هستند و از طریق دروازه به Ironwood مهاجرت می‌کنند. کیف‌پول‌ها این کار را برای شما انجام می‌دهند، هرچند بیشتر آن‌ها به شما تا حدی

title: What Are Zcash TEX Addresses?
description: A Zcash TEX address is a special type of receiving address. TEX stands for "Transparent Exchange". It is a Bech32m re-encoding of a single p2pkh Transparent…
text: What Are Zcash TEX Addresses? TL;DR A TEX address is a transparent Zcash address written in a different format. It starts with tex1 and is defined in ZIP 320. It tells your wallet one thing: pay this address with transparent funds only. If your balance is shielded, a compatible wallet does two steps for you. It moves the amount to a temporary transparent address, then sends it to the TEX address. In 2023, Binance asked the Zcash community for a way to refuse shielded deposits and send them back. TEX addresses are the answer, and Binance is the exchange on the ZecHub Custodial Exchanges list that takes TEX deposits. Support has grown on the sending side too: Coinbase lets its users send ZEC to TEX addresses, and wallet toolkits have been adding ZIP 320 support. A payment to a TEX address is public on the blockchain, like any transparent payment. The rest of your shielded balance stays private. Core Explanation A Zcash TEX address is a special type of receiving address. TEX stands for "Transparent Exchange". It is a Bech32m re-encoding of a single p2pkh Transparent address. TEX addresses start with tex1 and are a separate type from Unified Addresses. A TEX address tells a compatible wallet to make a Transparent-Only (T -> T) transaction. The logic is as follows: When a compatible wallet detects a TEX Address, it decodes it to obtain the Transparent receiver it contains. The wallet then sends the required funds for the tx from the Shielded pool to a separate, user-controlled, ephemeral Transparent address (Z -> T). It then sends those funds to the decoded Transparent receiver of the TEX address (T -> T). The technical proposal for TEX addresses is outlined in Zcash ZIP 320, which defines an address type exclusively for receiving funds from Transparent Addresses. How widely are TEX addresses used? Adoption is still partial, but it is no longer limited to a single exchange. Two different roles are worth separating: Issuing TEX deposit addresses. Binance is the exchange on our Custodial Exchanges list that hands out a TEX address for deposits, so that funds arrive from a transparent source (ZIP 320, Background). ZIP 320 does not expect other exchanges to issue TEX addresses unless they need to know which address a payment came from. Sending to TEX addresses. This is the side that has grown. In October 2024, Coinbase announced that Coinbase.com users can send Zcash to TEX addresses (Coinbase Assets announcement). Wallet toolkits have been adding ZIP 320 support as well: KeepKey added signing for TEX transactions on firmware 7.15 (keepkey/hdwallet #75), and the XChainJS zcash-js library was patched after it rejected valid tex1 recipients (more on that below). So TEX addresses are not universal, but a reader should no longer assume Binance is the only place they appear. When Do I Need a TEX Address You need a TEX address when sending funds to a Transparent address using a wallet that does not support sending directly to a Transparent address. Certain wallets don't allow sending directly to a Transparent address, and the recipient may not provide a TEX equivalent. So, converting from a Transparent to a TEX address may be required at times. This can be achieved manually by running the reference implementation outlined in zip-320. You need a TEX address when sending funds to a centralized exchange that requires those funds to come from a Transparent source. Binance is the reason TEX addresses exist. In November 2023, it told the Zcash community that ZEC could be delisted unless there was a way to refuse deposits from shielded addresses and send them back to the depositor (ZIP 320, Background). ZIP 320 does not expect other exchanges to issue TEX addresses unless they need to know which address a payment came from. Binance is the exchange on our Custodial Exchanges list that takes deposits to a TEX address. TEX addresses inform a compatible wallet that all the funds sent to that address must be transparent and exclude every shielded value

title: تراکنش‌ها
description: ZEC یک دارایی دیجیتال پرکاربرد برای پرداخت است که ویژگی‌های قدرتمند حریم خصوصی را ارائه می‌دهد و آن را برای تراکنش‌های گوناگونی مانند پرداخت به دوستان، خرید…
text: تراکنش‌ها ZEC یک دارایی دیجیتال پرکاربرد برای پرداخت است که ویژگی‌های قدرتمند حریم خصوصی را ارائه می‌دهد و آن را برای تراکنش‌های گوناگونی مانند پرداخت به دوستان، خرید کردن یا اهدا مناسب می‌سازد. برای به حداکثر رساندن حریم خصوصی و امنیت، ضروری است که بدانید انواع مختلف تراکنش‌ها در Zcash چگونه کار می‌کنند. خلاصه Zcash از دو نوع تراکنش پشتیبانی می‌کند: محافظت‌شده، که جزئیات را خصوصی نگه می‌دارد، و شفاف، که آن‌ها را به‌صورت عمومی ثبت می‌کند. آدرس‌های محافظت‌شده با u یا z آغاز می‌شوند. آدرس‌های شفاف با t آغاز می‌شوند و رفتاری بسیار شبیه به یک آدرس Bitcoin دارند. در هر پرداخت، انتخاب با شماست. حریم خصوصی گزینه‌ای است که Zcash در اختیار شما قرار می‌دهد، نه تنظیمی که شخص دیگری به جای شما تعیین کند. برداشت از صرافی رایج‌ترین جایی است که افراد حریم خصوصی خود را از دست می‌دهند. اگر صرافی فقط از برداشت شفاف پشتیبانی می‌کند، پس از رسیدن وجوه، خودتان آن‌ها را محافظت‌شده کنید. کارمزدها از ZIP 317 پیروی می‌کنند و با اندازهٔ تراکنش افزایش می‌یابند. کیف‌پول‌هایی که هنوز کارمزد ثابت قدیمی را ارسال می‌کنند ممکن است با تأخیر در تراکنش‌های خود مواجه شوند. بیشتر تراکنش‌های Zcash طبق ZIP 203 دارای ارتفاع انقضا هستند. اگر یک تراکنش پیش از استخراج منقضی شود، پس از آن ارتفاع انقضا نمی‌تواند تأیید شود و ممکن است لازم باشد دوباره ارسال شود. تراکنش‌های محافظت‌شده --- تراکنش‌های محافظت‌شده زمانی رخ می‌دهند که شما ZEC را به کیف‌پول محافظت‌شدهٔ خود منتقل می‌کنید. آدرس کیف‌پول محافظت‌شدهٔ شما با u یا z آغاز می‌شود. هنگام ارسال تراکنش‌های محافظت‌شده، شما و کسانی که با آن‌ها تراکنش انجام می‌دهید می‌توانید سطحی از حریم خصوصی را حفظ کنید که در شبکه‌های پرداختی که به‌طور پیش‌فرض عمومی هستند امکان‌پذیر نیست. ارسال یک تراکنش محافظت‌شده زمانی ساده‌تر است که از کیف‌پولی استفاده کنید که از شبکهٔ فعلی Zcash و استخرهای محافظت‌شدهٔ فعلی پشتیبانی می‌کند. پیش از آنکه برای حریم خصوصی به یک کیف‌پول تکیه کنید، بررسی کنید که آیا از ارسال محافظت‌شده، دریافت محافظت‌شده و استخری که قصد استفاده از آن را دارید پشتیبانی می‌کند یا خیر. هنگام برداشت ZEC از یک صرافی، بررسی کنید که آیا آن صرافی از برداشت محافظت‌شده پشتیبانی می‌کند یا برداشت شفاف. اگر فقط از برداشت شفاف پشتیبانی می‌کند، پس از رسیدن وجوه، آن‌ها را به کیف‌پولی که از تراکنش محافظت‌شده پشتیبانی می‌کند منتقل کنید. استفاده از تراکنش‌های محافظت‌شده برای ارسال و دریافت وجوه بهترین راه برای حفظ حریم خصوصی و کاهش خطر نشت داده‌های پرداخت است. تراکنش‌های شفاف تراکنش‌های شفاف مشابه تراکنش‌های Bitcoin کار می‌کنند. جزئیات تراکنش، از جمله آدرس‌های شفاف و مقادیر شفاف، به‌صورت عمومی روی بلاک‌چین قابل مشاهده است. هنگامی که حریم خصوصی در اولویت است، باید از تراکنش‌های شفاف پرهیز کرد. آدرس‌های شفاف همچنان در برخی موقعیت‌ها مفید هستند، به‌ویژه زمانی که یک صرافی یا سرویس از آدرس‌های محافظت‌شده پشتیبانی نمی‌کند. اگر ZEC را در یک آدرس شفاف دریافت می‌کنید، پیش از انجام پرداخت‌های بعدی، محافظت‌شده کردن آن را در نظر بگیرید. راهی ساده برای تصور آن یک تراکنش شفاف مانند یک کارت‌پستال است. نامه‌رسان آن را تحویل می‌دهد، اما هر کسی که در طول مسیر آن را در دست بگیرد می‌تواند پیام را بخواند، ببیند چه کسی آن را فرستاده و چه کسی آن را دریافت می‌کند. یک تراکنش محافظت‌شده مانند یک پاکت مهروموم‌شده است. سرویس پست همچنان تأیید می‌کند که یک نامهٔ واقعی با تمبر واقعی از سیستم عبور کرده است، و هیچ‌کس نمی‌تواند نامه‌ای جعل کند یا یک نامه را دو بار بفرستد. محتوای پاکت میان فرستنده و گیرنده باقی می‌ماند. نکتهٔ مهم این است که Zcash به شما اجازه می‌دهد برای هر پرداخت تصمیم بگیرید کدام‌یک را ارسال کنید. کارمزدهای Zcash اجازه دهید کیف‌پول شما کارمزد شبکه را محاسبه کند و پیش از ارسال، آن را بررسی کنید. کارمزدها به ZEC پرداخت می‌شوند: 1 ZEC = 100,000,000 زاتوشی. کارمزد به دلار آمریکا به نرخ تبدیل ZEC نیز بستگی دارد. چرا دو پرداخت می‌توانند کارمزدهای متفاوتی داشته باشند ZIP 317 کارمزد متعارف را بر اساس کنش‌های منطقی محاسبه می‌کند، نه درصدی از مبلغ ارسالی: کنش‌های منطقی اجزای تراکنش را می‌سنجند. برای مثال، یک تراکنش صرفاً Orchard از تعداد کنش‌های Orchard خود استفاده می‌کند؛ یک تراکنش صرفاً Sapling از بزرگ‌ترِ تعداد ورودی‌های خرج و تعداد خروجی‌های خود استفاده می‌کند. سهم استخرهای مختلف با هم جمع می‌شود. اجزای شفاف از محاسبه‌ای مبتنی بر اندازه استفاده می‌کنند. برای فرمول کامل، ا

title: یادداشت‌ها
description: هنگام ارسال یک تراکنش Z2Z (محافظت‌شده به محافظت‌شده)، شما می‌توانید یک یادداشت (پیام) در تراکنش قرار دهید. این یادداشت را می‌توان برای چندین کار مختلف به کار…
text: یادداشت‌ها خلاصه یادداشت پیام کوتاهی است که شما به پرداختی که به یک آدرس محافظت‌شده ارسال می‌شود پیوست می‌کنید. این پیام رمزنگاری شده است، بنابراین کسانی که بلاک‌چین را زیر نظر دارند نمی‌توانند آن را بخوانند. فیلد یادداشت تا 512 بایت متن را در خود جای می‌دهد. افراد از یادداشت‌ها برای اعلام اینکه چه کسی پرداخت را فرستاده و برای چه بوده است، یا برای ارسال یک پیام خصوصی استفاده می‌کنند. پرداخت‌ها به آدرس‌های شفاف نمی‌توانند یادداشت داشته باشند. یک لینک درخواست پرداخت می‌تواند یادداشت را برای شما پر کند تا یک فروشگاه بتواند هر سفارش را برچسب‌گذاری کند. توضیح اصلی ارسال یادداشت‌های رمزنگاری‌شده هنگام ارسال یک تراکنش Z2Z (محافظت‌شده به محافظت‌شده)، شما می‌توانید یک یادداشت (پیام) در تراکنش قرار دهید. این یادداشت را می‌توان برای چندین کار مختلف به کار برد. امضای تراکنش‌ها یادداشت‌ها در درجه اول برای امضای پرداخت‌ها استفاده می‌شوند. از آنجا که تراکنش‌های محافظت‌شده داده‌های شما را رمزنگاری می‌کنند، شما نمی‌توانید ببینید چه کسی ZEC را برایتان فرستاده و ZEC ممکن است برای چه بوده باشد. کاربران می‌توانند از فیلد یادداشت برای امضای نام یا نام مستعار خود استفاده کنند تا طرف مقابل بداند تراکنش از طرف چه کسی بوده است. آن‌ها همچنین می‌توانند توضیح دهند که تراکنش برای چه بوده است. ارسال پیام کاربرد دیگر یادداشت رمزنگاری‌شده، ارسال پیام به کسی است که یک z-addr دارد. این پیام‌ها می‌توانند درباره هر چیزی باشند، چه یک یادآوری به یک دوست و چه یک پیام حساس که باید تا حد ممکن خصوصی بماند. نامه‌های عاشقانه روی بلاک‌چین شخصی بود که در یکی از نخستین بلوک‌های بلاک‌چین Zcash یک نامه عاشقانه برای شریک زندگی‌اش فرستاد. فردی متوجه شد که شریک زندگی‌اش از طریق یک یادداشت Zcash فایلی برایش فرستاده است. این فایل بلیتی برای یک رویداد ویژه در خارج از کشور بود که او و معشوق دوردستش درباره شرکت در آن با هم صحبت کرده بودند. آن یادداشت یک نامه عاشقانه بود. تصویرسازی / تمثیل یک پرداخت محافظت‌شده را مانند پاکتی مهر و موم‌شده با پول درون آن تصور کنید. یادداشت، کاغذی است که همراه پول تا شده و درون پاکت قرار گرفته است. بلاک‌چین اداره پست است. پاکت را حمل می‌کند و ثبت می‌کند که به مقصد رسیده است، و هرگز آن را باز نمی‌کند. کسی که پاکت را باز می‌کند، پیام را می‌خواند. یک پرداخت شفاف مانند کارت‌پستال است، بنابراین پاکتی وجود ندارد که پیامی را درون آن بگذارید. بررسی عمیق چه چیزی در یک یادداشت جا می‌شود فیلد یادداشت همیشه دقیقاً 512 بایت است. یک یادداشت متنی کوتاه‌تر پیش از رمزنگاری با بایت‌های صفر پر می‌شود، بنابراین همه یادداشت‌ها در on-chain هم‌اندازه به نظر می‌رسند. بیشتر یادداشت‌ها متن ساده UTF-8 هستند. ZIP 302 همچنین یادداشت‌هایی را که با بایتی با مقدار 0xF5 یا بالاتر شروع می‌شوند برای انواع دیگر داده رزرو می‌کند، و یادداشتی که با 0xF6 شروع شود و پس از آن صفرها بیایند به معنای «بدون یادداشت» است. هر خروجی محافظت‌شده در یک تراکنش یادداشت خودش را دارد، بنابراین یک تراکنش که به چند نفر پرداخت می‌کند می‌تواند برای هر یک از آن‌ها پیام متفاوتی داشته باشد. پیشرفته تاریخی. این دمو دیگر به شکلی که نوشته شده اجرا نمی‌شود. دموی زیر از zcashd استفاده می‌کند و اسکریپت دریافت آن یادداشت‌ها را از طریق zcash-cli می‌خواند. zcashd در 18 July 2026 به توقف خودکار پایان پشتیبانی رسید، بنابراین آن اسکریپت نمی‌تواند به یک نود در حال اجرا دسترسی پیدا کند، و این اسکریپت منتقل نشده است. خواندن یادداشت‌های محافظت‌شده از خط فرمان همچنان روی Zallet کار می‌کند: zallet rpc zlistunspent هر note محافظت‌شده دریافتی را با همان فیلد memoStr که اسکریپت می‌خواند برمی‌گرداند. برای دیدن این فرمان به راهنمای مرجع سریع Zallet مراجعه کنید، و برای انتقال یک نود از zcashd به راهنمای مهاجرت به Zebra و Zallet مراجعه کنید. Zallet هنوز در مرحله بتا است. این بخش به عنوان یک سند تاریخی از دموی Magic-Wormhole نگه داشته شده است. در اینجا نحوه استفاده از یادداشت‌های محافظت‌شده Zcash همراه با Magic-Wormhole CLI و zcashd برای ارسال امن فایل‌ها از یک کامپیوتر به کامپیوتر دیگر آمده است! صفحات مرتبط URIهای درخواست پرداخت: یک یادداشت را در لینک یا کد QR zcash: قرار دهید. تراکنش‌ها: انواع تراکنش‌های محافظت‌شده و شفاف. استخرهای محافظت‌شده: جایی که noteهای محافظت‌شده‌ای که یادداشت‌ها را حمل می‌کنند قرار دارند. کیف‌پول‌ها: از فیلتر Shielded Memo استفاده کنید تا کیف‌پول‌هایی را که از یادداشت پشتیبانی می‌کنند پیدا کنید. راهنمای مرجع سریع

title: Mobile Top-ups with Zcash
description: Recharge a prepaid phone with ZEC, with or without creating an account.
text: Mobile Top-ups with Zcash Recharge a prepaid phone with ZEC, with or without creating an account. TL;DR You can buy prepaid mobile airtime with ZEC from online gift-card shops such as Coinsbee and CardsRelay. Coinsbee needs an account. CardsRelay needs only an email address for the confirmation. Both show you the exact ZEC amount and a payment address at checkout. Send exactly that amount before the invoice expires. Memos only reach shielded addresses. If a payment address is transparent, a memo will not be delivered, so keep your order ID for any refund request. Top-ups usually work only for prepaid numbers. Check the number and the network before you pay. Core Explanation A mobile top-up adds airtime or data credit to a prepaid phone number. Several shops that sell gift cards for crypto also sell top-ups for hundreds of mobile networks around the world, and some of them accept ZEC. The flow is the same everywhere: choose the country and network, enter the phone number and amount, pay the invoice in ZEC, and wait for the credit to arrive. Below are two options: Coinsbee (account required) and CardsRelay (no account). Option 1: Coinsbee (account required) Create an account Visit Coinsbee.com and create an account. Select your country and network Select your country in the top left corner, choose mobile phone credit, and select the network you want to top up (for example, MTN). Fill in details and purchase Enter the phone number and amount, then click "Buy Now". Open the cart to view your order, click continue, and choose ZEC as the payment method. Payment details The invoice shows the amount in ZEC and the address the funds should be sent to. In the example below, the address is transparent. Send the payment Copy the amount and address carefully and send the full amount before the invoice countdown ends. An underpaid or expired invoice is not fulfilled. Do not rely on the memo field for refunds: memos are only delivered to shielded addresses, and a payment to a transparent address carries no memo. Instead, keep your order ID. Coinsbee invoices are handled by a payment provider, and its help center explains how to request a refund from that provider if an order is underpaid or expires. Processing Once the payment is confirmed, the order is usually processed within a few minutes. Confirmation The credit arrives on the phone line. If you confirm your email during checkout, you also get an email once the order is complete. Option 2: CardsRelay (no account) If you would rather not create an account, CardsRelay sells mobile top-ups for ZEC without registration. Choose your country and operator Visit CardsRelay and open the Mobile Top Ups section. Over 750 operators are supported globally. Enter the number and amount Fill in the mobile number to be credited and choose the top-up value. The price shown is a single all-in total, with no separate exchange-rate markup added later. Enter your email An email address is required so the confirmation can be delivered, and it is verified before the order is placed. No account is created and no identity documents are requested. Pay with ZEC Select Zcash at checkout. ZEC is accepted directly rather than converted by a third party. A payment address and the exact amount are shown. Confirmation The top-up is processed and confirmation arrives by email, usually within seconds. CardsRelay also sells gift cards for around 2,500 brands, and accepts Monero and Zano alongside Zcash. It is operated by Payzy ME FZ Ltd. Troubleshooting The credit never arrived. Top-ups usually work only for prepaid numbers. Check the number for typos, and make sure you picked the right network (a recently ported number may still show the old one). The order was refunded instead of fulfilled. Some networks limit how many top-ups a number can receive per day or month, and networks sometimes have outages. Try again later or contact the shop's support. The invoice expired or was underpaid. The shop does not fulfill the order.

title: Zcash Payment Request URIs
description: A payment request URI is a zcash: link defined by ZIP 321. Compatible wallets read the address, amount, and optional memo from the link or QR and prefill a…
text: Zcash Payment Request URIs TL;DR A payment request URI is a link that starts with zcash: and carries the details of a payment: the address, the amount, and an optional memo. Shared as a QR code or a clickable link, it lets your wallet fill in the payment for you. You check the details and approve. ZIP 321 defines the format. It grew out of Bitcoin's BIP 21. One request can pay several recipients in a single transaction. ZecHub hosts a payment widget and a generator, so a shop can add a Zcash payment button without writing the URI by hand. Core Explanation A payment request URI is a zcash: link defined by ZIP 321. Compatible wallets read the address, amount, and optional memo from the link or QR and prefill a transaction. No extra accounts, no processor in the middle. Open payment widget Build a payment request The widget demo is a live ZIP-321 modal: QR, copy address/URI, short link, and Open in Wallet. The tools page is the generator if you want to set your own address and amount first. Anatomy Field Required Notes --- --- --- address yes Prefer a Unified Address (u1 / utest1) amount no Decimal ZEC with . as the separator and at most 8 decimal places (0.5, not 0,5) memo no Shielded addresses only. The memo's UTF-8 bytes (at most 512), base64url-encoded without = padding: Thanks! becomes VGhhbmtzIQ, not the plain text label no Human-readable name shown by some wallets. Percent-encode spaces and reserved characters (Coffee%20shop); a + is a literal plus, not a space Full rules: ZIP 321. Use cases Checkout: prefill price and an order memo so the customer only confirms in their wallet Invoices: share one link or QR Donations: embed the widget on a site P2P: send a zcash: link in chat Embed on a site Point this script at your own shielded address. Hosted copy lives on ZecHub: Required: data-address, data-amount, data-target. Try the hosted button first: Open payment widget. Videos How to make Payment Requests with Zcash: Adding a Zcash Donation Widget to your Website: Visual / Analogy Think of a bank transfer form with fields for the account number, the amount, and a note saying what the payment is for. Filling it in by hand is slow, and one wrong digit sends the money to the wrong place. A payment request URI is that form, filled in by the shop. The QR code is a photo of the form. Your phone camera reads the photo, the wallet copies every field into place, and you check the numbers and sign. A link on a web page does the same job. Clicking it hands the filled form to your wallet. Deep Dive A real example Here is an example from ZIP 321, written for testnet: It asks for 1 ZEC to one shielded Sapling address. The memo decodes to "This is a simple memo." The message "Thank you for your purchase" is the text the wallet shows on screen. Rules a wallet checks The amount format is strict. amount=0.5 and amount=50 are valid. amount=50,000.00, amount=.5, and amount=0.123456789 are invalid: a period is the only decimal separator, and there can be at most 8 digits after it. No amount can exceed 21,000,000 ZEC. In the raw URI, the memo is encoded in base64url, and it can hold up to 512 bytes once decoded. A memo attached to a transparent address makes the whole request invalid, because transparent addresses cannot carry memos. Sprout addresses are not allowed at all, and a request that does not follow the ZIP 321 grammar must be rejected. Two more fields exist beyond the table above. message is a description of the payment for the wallet to display. req-asset is reserved for Custom Assets, as defined in ZIP 227. Paying several people at once Each extra payment gets an index number added to its parameter names, for example address.1, amount.1 and memo.1. The wallet builds one transaction that pays everyone on the list. This is useful for a checkout that splits a payment, or for a group of donations sent together. Where the format came from Bitcoin has two older standards for payment requests: BIP 21, a simple link for one recipient, and BIP 7

title: بازیابی وجوه کیف‌پول Zcash
description: عبارت‌های بازیابی، کلیدهای خرج‌کننده، کلیدهای مشاهده و فایل‌های کیف‌پول جایگزین یکدیگر نیستند. یک عبارت بازیابی می‌تواند کلیدهای کیف‌پول را برای کیف‌پول‌های…
text: بازیابی وجوه کیف‌پول Zcash چرا باید مواد بازیابی خود را نگه دارید؟ عبارت‌های بازیابی، کلیدهای خرج‌کننده، کلیدهای مشاهده و فایل‌های کیف‌پول جایگزین یکدیگر نیستند. یک عبارت بازیابی می‌تواند کلیدهای کیف‌پول را برای کیف‌پول‌های بسیاری استخراج کند، اما جایگزین هر کلید یا فایل کیف‌پول قدیمی نمی‌شود. یک کلید مشاهده می‌تواند فعالیت محافظت‌شده را آشکار کند، اما نمی‌تواند خرج کردن را مجاز کند. بازیابی به داشتن اختیار خرج صحیح و یک مسیر پشتیبانی‌شده فعلی برای استخری که وجوه را نگه می‌دارد بستگی دارد. مواد بازیابی را خصوصی نگه دارید و هرگز عبارت‌های بازیابی، کلیدهای خرج‌کننده یا فایل‌های کیف‌پول را با کسی که به او اعتماد ندارید به اشتراک نگذارید. امنیت و مسئولیت بسیار مهم است که کاربران خطرات مربوط به کار با کلیدهای خصوصی را درک کنند و این کلیدها را از دسترسی غیرمجاز محافظت کنند. امنیت وجوه به مسئولیت کاربر در حفاظت از کلیدهای خصوصی خود بستگی دارد. وجوه محافظت‌شده قدیمی: Sprout، Sapling و Orchard ممکن است لازم باشد ZEC محافظت‌شده قدیمی‌تر به‌عنوان بخشی از بازیابی مهاجرت داده شود. مسیر به این بستگی دارد که در حال حاضر کدام استخر محافظت‌شده وجوه را نگه می‌دارد. NU7 برای 5 نوامبر 2026 برنامه‌ریزی شده است. پس از فعال شدن آن، مسیر فعلی مهاجرت از استخر قدیمی Sprout دیگر کار نخواهد کرد. اگر هنوز ZEC در استخر Sprout دارید، پیش از ارتقا آن را مهاجرت دهید. پس از فعال‌سازی، ابزارهای موجود دیگر قادر نخواهند بود وجوه Sprout را به Sapling، آدرس‌های شفاف یا هر مقصد دیگری منتقل کنند. اگر این صفحه را پس از فعال شدن NU7 مشاهده می‌کنید، Sprout در یخ منجمد شده است تا زمانی که یک روش بازیابی در آینده در دسترس قرار گیرد، که در حال حاضر برنامه‌ریزی نشده است. پاسخ در یک صفحه وجوه شما در اینجاست مسیر مهاجرت چه باید بکنید --- --- --- Sprout Sprout → Sapling → Ironwood اگر wallet.dat یا یک کلید خرج‌کننده مستقل Sprout دارید، ابتدا مسیر بازیابی فعلی Argos را امتحان کنید. اگر Argos مناسب نیست، از مسیر sidecar قدیمی در راهنمای میدانی کامل استفاده کنید. Sprout باید ابتدا به Sapling برسد و سپس به Ironwood منتقل شود. این مسیر به دلیل NU7 به زمان حساس است. Sapling Sapling → Ironwood به هیچ محیط بازیابی Sprout نیازی نیست. از یک کیف‌پول فعلی استفاده کنید که هم بتواند حساب Sapling مشخص شما را بازیابی یا خرج کند و هم تراکنش‌های Ironwood بسازد. پشتیبانی از Ironwood به‌تنهایی پشتیبانی از بازیابی Sapling قدیمی را ثابت نمی‌کند. Orchard Orchard → Ironwood Orchard فقط برای خروج است. از جریان مهاجرت داخلی Orchard به Ironwood در یک کیف‌پول سازگار فعلی استفاده کنید. به وجوه بازیابی‌شده و استخر Ironwood مراجعه کنید. جریان تصمیم‌گیری پنج‌پرسشی آیا Sprout است؟ یک عبارت بازیابی به‌تنهایی به یک مسیر بازیابی مربوط به دوره‌های بعدی Sapling/Orchard اشاره دارد، نه Sprout. یک آدرس zc...، یا یک کیف‌پول بازیابی‌شده که موجودی Sprout گزارش می‌کند، به Sprout اشاره دارد. چه مواد بازیابی‌ای دارید؟ به دنبال wallet.dat، کامپیوتر قدیمی یا datadir، یک نسخه پشتیبان zexportwallet یا یک کلید خرج‌کننده Sprout صادرشده بگردید. یک آدرس zc... به‌تنهایی کافی نیست. Argos یا sidecar قدیمی؟ اگر wallet.dat یا یک کلید خرج‌کننده مستقل Sprout دارید و فقط می‌خواهید وجوه را خارج کنید، ابتدا Argos را امتحان کنید. اگر Argos نمی‌تواند این مواد را پردازش کند یا اگر می‌خواهید کل مجموعه بازیابی تحت کنترل خودتان باشد، از مسیر sidecar قدیمی در راهنمای میدانی کامل استفاده کنید. آیا از قبل یک datadir همگام‌سازی‌شده و هرس‌نشده zcashd دارید؟ این موضوع فقط برای مسیر sidecar قدیمی اهمیت دارد. داده‌های نود موجود را فقط پس از یک خاموش‌سازی تمیز کپی کنید؛ در غیر این صورت، راهنمای میدانی گزینه‌های snapshot/از صفر را پوشش می‌دهد. وجوه در نهایت به کجا می‌رسند؟ Ironwood. Sprout ابتدا از Sapling عبور می‌کند، زیرا هیچ تراکنش مستقیم و واحدی از Sprout به Ironwood وجود ندارد. در Sapling متوقف نشوید. راهنمای میدانی کامل مهاجرت از استخر ZEC برای مرجع کامل مهاجرت، شامل مسیرهای بازیابی دقیق، دستورات، کارمزدها، الزامات سخت‌افزاری، ملاحظات حریم خصوصی، عیب‌یابی و یادداشت‌های منابع، راهنمای کامل را بخوانید. نسخه 1.1 · به‌روزشده در 18 سپتامبر 2026 راهنمای میدانی کامل مهاجرت از استخر ZEC را در ZecHub بخوانید پیش از شروع: ابتدا مشخص کنید چه چیزی را بازیابی می‌کنید و چه مواد بازیابی‌ای هنوز در اختیار دارید. یک عبارت بازیابی کیف‌پول فعلی یا یک کلید خرج‌کننده غیر

title: Zcash Tools for Creators: Tipping & Profile Platforms
description: A comprehensive guide to privacy-preserving tipping and profile tools built on Zcash for content creators, cypherpunks, and the privacy-conscious community.
text: Zcash Tools for Creators: Tipping & Profile Platforms A comprehensive guide to privacy-preserving tipping and profile tools built on Zcash for content creators, cypherpunks, and the privacy-conscious community. --- Table of Contents Zcash.me TIPZ Why Privacy Matters for Creators Visual / Analogy Related Pages --- TL;DR Two Zcash tools help creators get paid privately. Zcash.me gives you a profile page with your shielded address, and TIPZ lets fans send you tips. With Zcash.me, you share one link, zcash.me/[username], that shows your unified address and your social accounts. With TIPZ, fans can tip in other cryptocurrencies, and every tip reaches you as shielded ZEC. Both tools ask for your unified address (u1...). Tips to a shielded address keep your income and balance out of public view. Core Explanation Zcash.me Overview Zcash.me is a profile directory and discovery platform that makes it easy for anyone to find and send ZEC to Zcash users. It serves as the "Linktree for Zcash" - a simple way to share your shielded address and social presence with a single link. Item Details ------------------- --------- Website https://zcash.me/ Twitter @zcashme Profile Format zcash.me/[username] Status Live (with features in development) Key Features Currently Available Custom Profile Pages - Personalized page with username, bio, avatar, and location Shielded Address Display - One-click copy button for your unified address Social Link Integration - X, LinkedIn, Telegram, and custom websites Verification System - Verified badge for community trust Referral Leaderboard - Track top referrers and community leaders Activity Status - Shows last active time. Coming Soon Feature Description -------------------- ------------- Location Map Find nearby Zcash users Platform Statistics View growth metrics Community Polls Vote on ecosystem topics News & Announcements Official updates Forum Community discussion Mobile App Full mobile experience Getting Started Visit https://zcash.me/ and click Join. Choose a unique username, add a bio and profile picture. Paste your Zcash unified address (u1...) Connect your social accounts. Share your link: zcash.me/[yourusername] --- TIPZ Overview TIPZ is a private tipping protocol purpose-built for creators and cypherpunks. Fans tip in any major cryptocurrency; it is automatically converted and delivered as shielded ZEC. Item Details ------------------- --------- Website https://tipz.cash/ Twitter @tipzcash Profile Format tipz.cash/@[username] Status Live "tipz.cash is a private tipping protocol for creators and cypherpunks." Why Privacy Matters for Creators Financial Freedom 0% platform fees Non-custodial & self-custody No middlemen Privacy-First Design Every tip arrives as shielded ZEC. Private wallet balance Encrypted messaging with tips Full creator anonymity option Cross-Chain Payments Currency Network ---------- --------- ETH Ethereum USDC Multiple chains SOL Solana ZEC Direct Zcash Creator Protection No deplatforming risk Censorship resistant No KYC required --- Visual / Analogy A tip jar on a café counter is glass. Everyone in the room sees who dropped in a coin and how full the jar is. A shielded address works like a locked mailbox with a slot. Fans drop in an envelope with a coin and a note, and only the creator opens the box. TIPZ adds a currency exchange at the door: a fan can arrive with ETH or SOL, and what lands in the mailbox is ZEC. Related Pages Unified Addresses: the u1... address both tools ask for. Wallets: pick a wallet to receive shielded tips. Memos: how a private note travels with a shielded payment. Payment Request URIs: a zcash: link or QR code that asks for a set amount. Payment Processors: tools for selling goods and services for ZEC. Last updated: October 2026

title: SOL/USDC to ZEC Swap Using encrypt.trade
description: Swap SOL or USDC on Solana into ZEC, with the cross-chain step routed through NEAR Intents.
text: SOL/USDC to ZEC Swap Using encrypt.trade Swap SOL or USDC on Solana into ZEC, with the cross-chain step routed through NEAR Intents. --- TL;DR encrypt.trade wraps SOL or USDC into encrypted tokens (eSOL/eUSDC), then swaps them to ZEC through NEAR Intents. Amounts are hidden on Solana, but your wallet address and its use of the app are public. ZEC is delivered to a transparent (t1/t3) address only, so it is visible on the Zcash chain until you shield it. Shield the ZEC in your wallet as soon as it arrives. The app and NEAR Intents both screen wallets for compliance. --- Core Explanation encrypt.trade is a Solana app run by JMD Labs Inc. It lets you swap SOL or USDC on Solana into Zcash (ZEC). Your tokens are first wrapped into encrypted versions so the amounts are hidden on Solana, then swapped to ZEC through NEAR Intents. The swap is private in some ways but not all. The app's own docs say your interaction with the chain is not anonymous: people can see that your wallet used the app, but not how much you moved. The ZEC also arrives at a transparent address, so it stays visible on the Zcash chain until you shield it. --- What to Know Before You Swap Solana side. Wrapping hides amounts, but your wallet address and its use of the app are public. Its best practices warn that a simple wrap, swap and unwrap makes your transaction linkable. Encryption. Encrypted balances are processed off-chain inside a hardware enclave (TEE). The developers' paper says this relies on TEE integrity, honest threshold key management and the cloud attestation root, not on cryptography alone. Cross-chain step. The swap to ZEC is routed through NEAR Intents, where independent solvers fill the order. Zcash side. NEAR Intents lists ZEC as supported for transparent addresses only, and the ZEC field on encrypt.trade only accepted transparent (t1 or t3) addresses when this guide was checked in September 2026. A transparent address shows its balance and incoming transfers publicly until you shield. Screening. The app checks connecting wallets against databases such as TRM and Chainalysis, and its compliance page says encrypted records can be reviewed if there is legitimate legal cause. NEAR Intents runs its own screening too. --- Step 1: Connect Your Solana Wallet Visit encrypt.trade using Chrome or Firefox, and connect your Phantom, Solflare, or Slope wallet. Ensure your wallet contains enough SOL for gas fees and the tokens you want to trade. Once connected, you're ready to wrap your assets. --- --- Step 2: Wrap Your Tokens Navigate to the Wrap section. Choose SOL or USDC, enter the amount, and confirm. The app locks your assets and issues encrypted versions (eSOL or eUSDC). Wrapping a different amount than you swap makes it harder to match the two by amount, but it does not hide that your wallet used the app. --- --- Step 3: Prepare Your ZODL Wallet Download ZODL, the Zcash wallet maintained by ZODL. On the Receive screen, copy your Zcash Transparent Address (it starts with t1). encrypt.trade does not accept shielded or unified addresses for ZEC at the moment. Save your seed phrase securely before proceeding. --- Step 4: Swap Back on encrypt.trade, go to Swap. Select eSOL/eUSDC -> ZEC, paste your ZODL transparent address, review details, and confirm. --- NEAR Intents handles the cross-chain routing and sends the ZEC to your ZODL wallet. It can take a few minutes. NEAR Intents suggests allowing up to 15 minutes for cross-chain swaps. --- Step 5: Shield Your ZEC Once the ZEC arrives, use ZODL's Shield option to move it into the shielded pool. Until then it sits at a transparent address where anyone can see the balance. Shielding protects what you do next, but the incoming transfer and the shielding transaction stay visible on chain. Always verify links, avoid reusing addresses, and test small amounts first. --- Who Is Involved and Where to Get Help encrypt.trade is the app, run by JMD Labs Inc. Its privacy policy says it collects technical data such as IP, bro

title: Non-Custodial Exchanges
description: In the ever-evolving world of cryptocurrency trading, non-custodial exchanges, also known as Decentralized Exchanges or DEXs, let users trade without handing…
text: Non-Custodial Exchanges TL;DR A non-custodial exchange lets you swap coins from your own wallet. You keep your private keys, and no exchange account holds your funds. Keeping your keys protects you from exchange hacks and failures. Privacy is a separate question. The deposit you send from another chain, such as Solana or Ethereum, is public on that chain. The swap service also sees your addresses and connection data. Some swap routes deliver ZEC to a transparent address, which is public. Your ZEC becomes private once it sits in a shielded address. Shield it in your own wallet before you spend it. Core Explanation Zcash Non-Custodial Exchanges In the ever-evolving world of cryptocurrency trading, non-custodial exchanges, also known as Decentralized Exchanges or DEXs, let users trade without handing their funds to an exchange account. You keep your own keys, but that does not mean nobody else is involved. Depending on the route, a swap can pass through a website or wallet app, a routing service, smart contracts, solvers and bridges. The exchanges listed above let you get and trade Zcash from your own wallet. How private a swap is depends on the service, the network you pay from, and whether your ZEC ends up in a shielded address. The sections below explain the difference. Understanding Non-Custodial Exchanges Non-custodial exchanges, also known as Decentralized Exchanges (DEXs), are platforms that facilitate cryptocurrency trading without requiring users to deposit their funds into the exchange itself. Instead, users keep control of their private keys and trade from their own wallets. Cross-chain swaps still rely on other parties to quote, route and settle the trade (see below). This can improve security, as users are not relying on the exchange to hold their assets, which reduces the risk of hacks or mismanagement. It does not make a swap private on its own. Transactions on non-custodial exchanges often use smart contracts, which are public, and the service you use can still see your addresses and connection details. A key advantage of non-custodial cryptocurrency exchanges lies in the increased control they provide to users over their assets. As these exchanges do not retain the assets, users enjoy complete ownership and authority over their digital currencies. Non-Custodial Exchanges Vs Custodial Exchanges #1 Security: Non-custodial exchanges remove the need to keep funds in a central exchange account. Users keep control of their private keys, reducing the risk of hacks, insider attacks and platform failures that custodial exchanges may experience. Cross-chain swaps can still hold funds for a short time in a deposit address or bridge while the trade settles. #2 Privacy: Non-custodial swaps usually do not need an exchange account, so you often skip signing up with an email or ID. That is not the same as anonymity. The deposit you send on the source network (for example, Solana or Ethereum) is public on that chain, and the service can still see your wallet addresses, IP address and swap details. Privacy on the Zcash side depends on where your ZEC lands (see below). #3 Decentralization: Non-custodial exchanges align more closely with the decentralized ethos of cryptocurrencies. Users have greater autonomy and control over their trading activities, in line with the broader principles of blockchain technology. When it comes to Custodial Exchanges, the level of Decentralization is often quite minimal in most centralized exchanges, which give rise to the exchange team or officials managing user data or information on the exchange. #4 Adaptability to Changing Regulations: Non-custodial exchanges are often more adaptable to changing regulatory environments. Since they do not hold user funds, they might have fewer compliance challenges compared to custodial exchanges. #5 Innovation and Experimentation: Non-custodial exchanges frequently drive innovation in the crypto space. They encourage the development of decentralized technologies,

title: Zcash Payment Processors
description: Ways to accept ZEC as a merchant, compared side by side. Every entry was checked against the provider's own site and API on 29 July 2026, apart from Zcash…
text: Zcash Payment Processors Ways to accept ZEC as a merchant, compared side by side. Every entry was checked against the provider's own site and API on 29 July 2026, apart from Zcash Payment Service, added on 1 November 2026. Support for privacy assets changes often, so each row carries its own verified date. If you are reading this months later, check the provider's site before you integrate. Processor Custody Shielded ZEC Self-host Merchant fee Regions / KYC Verified :-- :-- :-- :-- :-- :-- :-- CipherPay Non-custodial Yes, Orchard via Unified Addresses Yes, open source 1% per payment, free if self-hosted No KYC, regions not stated 2026-07-29 BTCPay Server Non-custodial, view key only Yes, shielded only (Sapling, Orchard, UA) Yes, open source None, you pay network fees only Global, no KYC 2026-07-29 Zcash Payment Service Non-custodial, incoming view key only Yes, shielded only (Sapling and Orchard) Yes, self-hosted only, open source None, you pay network fees only No account, no KYC 2026-11-01 ZGo Non-custodial Yes, Sapling and Orchard No, hosted service Prepaid session, price not published No KYC stated, regions not stated 2026-07-29 Flexa Customer self-custody, merchant settles in fiat Customer spends shielded, receiving side not documented No 1% per payment US and 37 SEPA countries, ZEC in EU unconfirmed 2026-07-29 NOWPayments Non-custodial by default No, transparent address only No 0.5%, or 1% with conversion Global except where prohibited, no KYC to start 2026-07-29 Plisio — payments suspended Custodial, despite marketing Not documented No 0.5% API, 1.5% white label No KYC to receive 2026-07-29 Binance Pay Custodial, off-chain No, shielded deposits rejected No Free wallet to wallet, 0.8% payouts Geo-restricted, ZEC delisted in FR, ES, IT, PL 2026-07-29 What the columns mean Custody is whether the processor holds your ZEC. Non-custodial means it goes to a wallet you control. Shielded ZEC is whether you can be paid into the shielded pool. Transparent only means the amount and addresses are public on the blockchain. Self-host is whether you can run the software yourself, with no company in the middle. Merchant fee excludes Zcash network fees, which someone pays in every case. Where a provider does not publish something, the entry says "not stated" or "not documented" rather than guessing. That is not the same as "no". Which one to pick For the most privacy and control, use BTCPay Server, a self-hosted CipherPay, or Zcash Payment Service if you can add a little code to your site. All three are shielded, open source, and hold no funds for you. For taking payments in a shop rather than online, use Flexa. For a hosted gateway where transparent payments are acceptable, use NOWPayments or Plisio. One caveat worth repeating: a transparent-only processor publishes every payment amount and address on the blockchain. And with any hosted non-custodial processor you hand over your viewing key, so the company can see your payments even though it cannot spend them. Self-hosting is the only way to avoid that. ZGo service warning, 29 July 2026. The ZGo backend at api.zgo.cash returned HTTP 503 on every endpoint while this page was being checked. The project is not abandoned and its maintainer was active in the community this month, but confirm the service is running before you rely on it. --- CipherPay Support Type: Shielded (Orchard, via Unified Addresses) Description: Accept Zcash in minutes, Non-custodial, Zero buyer data, No middleman. URL: CipherPay You give CipherPay a view-only key, so payments go straight to your own wallet and it never holds funds. It uses a fresh address for every invoice. Orchard only. There is no Sapling or transparent support, even though the repository README mentions Sapling. It costs 1% per payment, and nothing at all if you run it yourself. The whole thing is open source, as a Rust binary with SQLite or as a Docker image. There is no KYC, and buyers do not need an account. Integrations cover Shopify, WooComme

title: Shielded Newsletter
description: Send a markdown note to a list of shielded addresses as Zcash memos, using Zallet. The recipient list and the note stay off transparent addresses.
text: Shielded Newsletter Send a markdown note to a list of shielded addresses as Zcash memos, using Zallet. The recipient list and the note stay off transparent addresses. A shielded newsletter is a series of shielded transactions. Each output pays a tiny amount to a recipient Unified Address and carries the next slice of the note in the memo field. Zallet builds and sends those transactions. Zebra and Zaino only provide chain data. The scripts live in site/tutorials/shieldedNewsletter. They were written for an early Zallet and are not safe to run as-is against the current release. This page is the updated procedure. Checked against Zallet v0.1.0-beta.3 and the Zallet book as of 7 October 2026. What you need Zebra fully synced, with RPC bound to localhost. Zaino synced against that Zebra node. Zallet v0.1.0-beta.3 or newer, wallet build, with its RPC bound to localhost. The book lists zsendmany as implemented. A numeric fee is rejected: if you pass fee, it must be null, because Zallet always uses the ZIP 317 fee. A funded account whose Unified Address can spend shielded funds. Recipient Unified Addresses. A memo on a transparent address is an error. Do not put a funded address or a cookie in the wiki or in a committed script. The current txBuilderFromFile.sh has a Unified Address hardcoded. Replace it locally and do not commit it. Configure Zallet Generate a config with the Zallet that you are running, then point it at Zebra and Zaino. The sample in the old tutorial uses asofversion = "0.0.0" and a personal home path. Treat that file as a snapshot, not a template. rpc help must list zsendmany, zgetoperationstatus, and zgetoperationresult. Bind RPC to 127.0.0.1 only. Recipient list One Unified Address per line, no quotes, no blank lines. The script reads daoAddresses.md. The old readme says daoAddress.md. That file is not in the repo, and the names do not match. Send one memo zsendmany is asynchronous. It returns an operation id. Poll zgetoperationstatus until the status is success or an error. A fixed 5 second sleep, which is what the script does, loses the result when the build takes longer. zgetoperationresult consumes the operation, so do not call it until the status is terminal. Fee is omitted. Zallet computes ZIP 317. Do not pass a number. The memo field is raw hex, 512 bytes maximum. ascii2hex encodes ASCII only. A note with any non-ASCII character fails. xxd or python3 -c 'import sys; sys.stdout.write(sys.stdin.buffer.read().hex())' handles UTF-8. Privacy policy defaults to FullPrivacy. That is the right default for a shielded recipient. Do not pass AllowFullyTransparent. Script defects These are in the tree as of 8 October 2026. Do not run shieldNewsletter.sh until they are fixed. [[ bytesInFile -lt 512 ]] is missing $. The single-memo branch never runs. The chunk loop stores hex, then hex2ascii decodes it, then txBuilderFromFile.sh encodes it again. The last chunk is not flushed unless a later line overflows 512. A long line is not split. It is sent whole and can exceed the 512-byte memo. txBuilderFromFile.sh calls ./zallet rpc with no config path, and expects the binary in the current directory. Use zallet -c rpc. toCurl.sh talks to Zebra on port 8232 with a cookie, and calls getinfo and sendmany. Zallet does not provide sendmany. The mine-wait loop also uses [[ chainHeight -gt temp ]] without $, so it does not wait. zgettotalbalance 0 true is passed as extra positional arguments. Check rpc help zgettotalbalance on the binary you run before using that call. Each chunk sends 0.0001 ZEC to every recipient. The ZIP 317 fee is on top. A long note to many addresses spends more than the dust amounts. After a fix A corrected runner should: Read the note as bytes and split on 512-byte boundaries, not on lines. Hex-encode each chunk once. Call zallet -c rpc zsendmany with the funded UA, the recipient array, and no fee argument. Poll zgetoperationstatus for that operation id. Record the txid only after success. The old tutorial pag

title: Got ZEC on Solana? Move it to shielded Zcash
description: This page is for you if ZEC showed up in your Solana wallet because you hold ZCAT, or another Solana token that pays its holders in ZEC. You don't need to sell…
text: Got ZEC on Solana? Move it to shielded Zcash This page is for you if ZEC showed up in your Solana wallet because you hold ZCAT, or another Solana token that pays its holders in ZEC. You don't need to sell anything to follow it. You'll move the ZEC you already have from Solana to a Zcash wallet and end up with it shielded. We ran every step below with a real transfer on 27 September 2026, starting with 0.00266336 ZEC in Phantom. The fees, times and screens on this page are what we saw. --- TL;DR ZEC in your Solana wallet is a Solana token (mint A7bd…QXaS) backed 1:1 by real ZEC that the NEAR OmniBridge holds on the Zcash chain — "paper ZEC" that lives on Solana's public ledger and can't be shielded there. The route is two steps: deposit the token on solswap.org (NEAR Intents), then withdraw on near.com to your wallet's shielded u1 address. Don't use Phantom's own Swap button — it can't help you. Use a wallet the ZecHub directory marks Ironwood: Ready, and keep a little SOL in Phantom for the Solana fee. Our real test (27 September 2026, 0.00266336 ZEC): deposit landed in 9 seconds, withdrawal took about 8 minutes, total cost 0.00025 ZEC + 0.0016 SOL. Safety line: only sign message requests on near.com/solswap.org with intents.near in the message, never type your seed phrase, and paste a u1, never a t1. Visual analogy ZEC on Solana works like a casino chip. It prices like cash, and the casino — the NEAR OmniBridge — promises real banknotes (native ZEC) to anyone who returns the chip. But the chip is just a row in the casino's ledger: everyone can see who holds it, and its value depends on the casino's systems staying sound. Withdrawing through near.com is walking to the cage and cashing the chip. Once the banknotes are in a shielded pool, they're in your own opaque wallet — nobody can see the amount or the holder anymore. --- What you actually hold The ZEC in your Solana wallet is a token on Solana, not coins on the Zcash network. The NEAR OmniBridge issues it and holds real ZEC on the Zcash chain to back it; the bridge has been live on Solana since October 2025. Its Solana leg runs on Wormhole messages and NEAR Chain Signatures, not on a Zcash light client, so the Solana side is only as sound as those two systems. People call it "paper ZEC". It tracks the price of ZEC, but every balance and every transfer sits on Solana's public ledger under your wallet address, and it can't be shielded while it stays there. Check that yours is the real token. In Phantom, tap ZEC and scroll to About Zcash. The contract address must be: Phantom shortens it to A7bd…QXaS, so compare the first and last characters, or look the full address up on Solscan. Any other "ZEC" token in your wallet, whatever its name or logo, isn't this one. Leave it alone. --- Why move it Shielded ZEC is the point of Zcash. When your ZEC sits in a shielded pool, the sender, the receiver and the amount of each payment are encrypted on the Zcash chain. Nobody browsing an explorer can see your balance. You already hold ZEC. Moving it into a Zcash wallet gets you the part that makes it Zcash, and it takes the bridge out of the picture: native ZEC in your own wallet doesn't depend on anyone honouring a redemption. Who can see your Zcash payment? explains exactly what stays hidden. --- Pick a Zcash wallet ZecHub doesn't pick one for you. Choose from the ZecHub wallet directory, and check two labels on the wallet's card before you install it: Ironwood: Ready. Ironwood is the pool new shielded ZEC goes into since the Ironwood upgrade on 28 July 2026. The older Orchard pool no longer accepts new funds. Automatic Shielding. Useful if a payment lands transparent: the wallet moves that ZEC into the shielded pool for you. Do not treat this label as a substitute for Ironwood: Ready. A wallet can have Automatic Shielding and still lack an Ironwood pool (Edge is in that state on the directory today). Most other wallets show a Shield button instead. Install the wallet from the link on its

title: How to Swap for ZEC in Phantom Wallet
description: Already holding ZEC on Solana (for example from a token that pays holders in ZEC)? Do not swap it. Move that token to a shielded Zcash wallet with Got ZEC on…
text: How to Swap for ZEC in Phantom Wallet Already holding ZEC on Solana (for example from a token that pays holders in ZEC)? Do not swap it. Move that token to a shielded Zcash wallet with Got ZEC on Solana? Move it to shielded Zcash. --- Native ZEC or a ZEC token? "ZEC" in Phantom can mean two different assets, so know which one you're paying for. Phantom's built-in Swap button gives you a token representation of ZEC on Solana (or another network Phantom supports). It is not native ZEC. It sits at your Phantom address, it has no Zcash shielded functionality, and a Zcash wallet can't see it or shield it. Native ZEC only exists on the Zcash blockchain and is sent to a Zcash address. To get it you need a service that asks for your Zcash address, like a swap inside ZODL, one of the options on the DEX page, or solswap.org followed by a withdrawal to your Zcash wallet (Step 8). Check before you pay Network: the ZEC you receive should be on the Zcash network. If it says Solana, Ethereum or Base, it's a token. Asset: native ZEC has no token contract or mint address. If yours shows one, it's a token. There are also plenty of look-alike "ZEC" tokens on Solana, so don't go by the name alone. The OmniBridge token on Solana is A7bdiYdS5GjqGFtxf17ppRHtDKPkkRqbKtR27dxvQXaS; that is still a token, not native ZEC. Address: native ZEC goes to a Zcash address, which starts with t1, u1 or zs. If the ZEC is being sent to your Phantom address, you're getting a token. --- Step 1: Open the Swap Interface Launch the Phantom app and visit solswap.org from the Phantom browser. Type the address yourself. The site runs on NEAR Intents and can send ZEC out to a Zcash address. Phantom's own Swap button also lists ZEC, but that gets you the token described above, not native ZEC. --- Step 2: Select Networks and Tokens for Depositing Choose your source network (e.g., Ethereum or Solana) then deposit for swapping. Select a base token like SOL, USDT, or USDC. Choose ZEC as your destination token. Ensure that Zcash is available through the swap interface. --- Step 3: Enter Amount & Review Quote Enter the amount you’d like to swap. Use the receive amount shown on solswap.org. That quote is the one that applies on this route. --- Step 4: Check Gas & Fees Keep enough of the source-chain gas token in Phantom to approve the deposit (SOL on Solana, ETH on Ethereum). Read the fee line on the solswap quote before you confirm. Phantom's built-in Swap uses its own fee schedule (historically a 0.85% Phantom fee plus network gas and a bridging fee). Those numbers do not apply to a solswap.org deposit. --- Step 5: Adjust Settings (Optional) On solswap.org, review slippage and the quoted minimum receive on that screen before you deposit. If you are looking at Phantom's own Swap sheet instead, you are on the token route from the top of this page. Close it and open solswap.org in the Phantom browser. --- Step 6: Confirm Swap Review all swap details on solswap.org. Confirm the deposit in Phantom. --- Step 7: Monitor Status Track the deposit in solswap.org activity until it shows Completed. The Solana or source-chain transaction ID is on that activity row and on the chain explorer for that network. --- Step 8: Withdraw Native ZEC to Your Zcash Wallet After the swap, your ZEC shows up in your solswap.org Account balance. It isn't on the Zcash network yet, and it isn't in Phantom either. Open a Zcash wallet the directory marks Ironwood: Ready. Copy a u1 your wallet labels as shielded. A t1 also works, but that deposit is public until you shield it. On solswap.org, go to Account and tap Withdraw. Pick ZEC, set the network to Zcash, paste the address and check the first and last characters before you confirm. If Received amount and Fee stay at "–" and the button does nothing, the balance is not lost. It sits in NEAR Intents under your Phantom key. title: Zcash Testnet
description: Zcash Testnet is a parallel blockchain to the real Zcash main network (Mainnet) that replicates the exact protocol, rules, and transaction logic - but with two…
text: Zcash Testnet What Is the Zcash Testnet? Zcash Testnet is a parallel blockchain to the real Zcash main network (Mainnet) that replicates the exact protocol, rules, and transaction logic - but with two key differences: Coins have no real monetary value - they're called TAZ, not ZEC, and are used only for testing. Network upgrades, tools, and software are tested here first before deployment on the real Zcash blockchain. In other words, the Testnet is like a sandbox or experimental environment where developers, auditors, and builders can try ideas without risking real money. Why Does Testnet Exist? Testnet is crucial for blockchain development because real blockchains like Zcash are immutable - once transactions are confirmed on the main network, they cannot be undone. Testnet provides a safe replica to experiment, test, and debug features before deploying to Mainnet. Uses of Testnet Software Development & Integration Developers building wallets, exchanges, mining software, or privacy tools can safely test them on Testnet. Capabilities include: Sending and receiving transactions Mining new blocks with zero-value TAZ coins Building user interfaces and APIs Testing transaction privacy features (transparent vs shielded) Example: Tools like zcashtxtool use Testnet to generate transactions and test Zcash shielded asset functionalities. Real-world scenario: A wallet developer can connect software to a Testnet RPC endpoint and simulate the full lifecycle - creating addresses, sending shielded transactions, and validating balances - before going live on Mainnet. Testing Network Upgrades Zcash upgrades its core protocol periodically (e.g., NU6.1, NU6.2 and Ironwood). Testnet activates new upgrades before Mainnet, allowing developers and the community to identify and fix bugs. Example: A new consensus rule or transaction type is first pushed to Testnet. After successful testing, it activates on Mainnet at a predetermined block height. Testing Node Implementations Zcash's maintained node is Zebra (the Rust-based node maintained by the Zcash Foundation) and the maintained wallet is Zallet. zcashd, the original node implementation, reached its automatic end-of-support halt on 18 July 2026 and is no longer maintained - see the zcashd to Zebra and Zallet migration guide. Testnet enables testing of nodes in real conditions without financial risk. Node developers can: Validate block propagation Test RPC interfaces Observe node behavior under load Test mining software interactions Learning & Education Beginners can learn Zcash features such as mining, creating shielded transactions, and using Unified Addresses. Community tutorials and documentation provide access to Testnet faucets, explorers, and guides. Real Testnet Use Cases Developer Testing (Wallet / App) Connect to Zcash Testnet Request TAZ from a faucet Send shielded transactions Verify privacy and UI stability No real ZEC is lost even if mistakes occur. Exchange Integration Testing Run a Testnet node Use Zebrad JSON-RPC endpoints to process transactions Test automated deposit/withdrawal logic Ensures safe production code and prevents financial loss. Mining Setup Trials Use mining templates Test block validation Observe mining rewards (TAZ only) Tune mining performance Prevents downtime or lost earnings when moving to Mainnet. Academic / Protocol Research Researchers can test innovations like stateless verification, zero-knowledge proof optimization, or other protocol experiments using Testnet. Advanced users can also run custom Testnets or regtest environments for specialized experiments. Key Differences Between Mainnet and Testnet Feature Mainnet Testnet ----------------------- ----------------- -------------------------- Value of coins Real ZEC TAZ (no monetary value) Risk Financial risk Safe for testing Protocol upgrades Production Early activation Mining rewards Real issuance Test reward only Network utility Live transactions Testing and development Common Misconceptions Testnet coins

title: Unified Addresses
description: One address for all of Zcash. Share it, and the sender's wallet finds the most private way to pay you.
text: Unified Addresses One address for all of Zcash. Share it, and the sender's wallet finds the most private way to pay you. TL;DR A unified address (UA) is one Zcash address that holds several receivers: Ironwood, Sapling, and transparent. Mainnet UAs start with u1. ZIP 316 defined them, and they arrived with the NU5 upgrade on May 31, 2022. The sender's wallet picks the most private pool that both wallets support. You never choose a pool yourself. Your UA kept working when the Ironwood pool went live in July 2026. You did not need to share a new address. Your wallet can make a fresh UA for each sender, and all of them pay into the same account. Core Explanation A unified address (UA) is a single Zcash address that bundles several receivers into one. Receivers are the parts of an address that accept funds in a specific value pool: Ironwood, Sapling, and transparent. A UA starts with u1 on mainnet and was defined in ZIP 316, introduced with the NU5 network upgrade on May 31, 2022. Before unified addresses, receiving ZEC meant thinking about address types. A zs address took Sapling funds, a t address took transparent funds, and sending between types took extra steps. A UA ends that. You share one address, and the wallets work out the rest. How it works When someone sends to your UA, their wallet reads the receivers inside it and picks the most private pool that both wallets support: If both wallets support the current shielded pool, the payment arrives shielded. Nothing public touches the chain. If the sender can only send from an older pool, the wallet falls back to the best receiver you both share, such as Sapling. If the sender can only send transparent funds, the payment lands in your UA's transparent receiver, and your wallet can shield it from there. You never manage this yourself. The address stays the same; the routing happens inside it. Why it matters now Zcash keeps upgrading. When the Ironwood pool activated with NU6.3 on July 28, 2026, UA holders didn't need a new address: wallets simply started picking the Ironwood receiver inside the addresses they already had. Users holding older standalone addresses had to migrate. UA holders did nothing. This is the design goal. New pools arrive with future network upgrades, and a unified address absorbs them without anyone re-sharing addresses or moving funds by hand. See Zcash value pools for the current pool lineup. A fresh address for every sender Wallets can generate many diversified unified addresses for one account. Each one pays into the same funds, but no two of them can be linked on-chain. Give a different UA to each person or service that pays you, and no pair of them can compare addresses to learn they pay the same wallet. Visual / Analogy Picture a front door with three mail slots. The newest slot drops letters into a locked safe (Ironwood). The second drops them into a locked drawer (Sapling). The third drops them onto an open tray that anyone can read through the window (transparent). The mail carrier is the sender's wallet. It uses the most private slot it fits through. You give out one address for the door, and when the house gets a new safe, the address on the door stays the same. Deep Dive Related tools Viewing keys. Every account has unified viewing keys that share what a UA receives (or everything it sends) without sharing spend authority. Prefixes uview and uivk. See viewing keys. TEX addresses. Some exchanges, currently Binance, require deposits to arrive from a transparent source. A TEX address (ZIP 320) is a transparent-only companion to your UA for exactly that case. See transparent exchange addresses. Payment requests. A UA can be embedded in a payment request URI with an amount and memo prefilled. See payment request URIs. Quick facts --- --- Prefix u1 (mainnet) Encoding bech32m Defined in ZIP 316 Introduced NU5, May 31, 2022 Contains Ironwood, Sapling, and transparent receivers Spending key One per account, shared by all of its UAs Check which wallets s

title: Zallet Quick Reference Guide
description: Zallet exposes its functionality through JSON-RPC, the same interface style the zcashd wallet used. Anything you want the wallet to do — check a balance…
text: Zallet Quick Reference Guide TL;DR Zallet is a full-node Zcash wallet written in Rust. It replaces the wallet that used to live inside zcashd. zcashd reached its End-of-Support halt on 18 July 2026 and no longer runs. Zebra now handles the node side; Zallet handles the wallet side. You drive Zallet from the command line with zallet rpc , much as you used zcash-cli before. Every argument after the command name must be valid JSON, which means string values keep their double quotes. Zallet is in beta. Commands can change between releases, and not every zcashd RPC has been ported across yet. Core Explanation Zallet exposes its functionality through JSON-RPC, the same interface style the zcashd wallet used. Anything you want the wallet to do — check a balance, create an account, send a shielded payment — is a command you pass to zallet rpc. Two things differ from the old zcash-cli habit and account for most early mistakes. First, arguments must be valid JSON rather than bare text, so a string argument carries its own quotation marks inside the shell quotes. Second, the set of available commands depends on which beta release you are running, so the list built into your binary is more reliable than any written page, including this one. To list all available RPCs: To get detailed help for a specific RPC: Important: Every argument after the method name must be valid JSON. String values must be written as "value" (including the double quotes). Common Mistakes Dropping the inner quotes on string arguments. zallet rpc validateaddress u1abc... fails, because the address has to arrive as JSON. It needs to be written '"u1abc..."'. Assuming every RPC exists here. Porting is still in progress. Some methods behave identically, some need different usage, and some will not be carried over at all. Treating this page as authoritative over your binary. Zallet is in beta and moves quickly. When a command here does not work, check zallet rpc help before assuming something is broken. Expecting Zallet to be a node. It is the wallet half of the pair. Zebra runs the node, and Zallet talks to it. Returns the OpenRPC schema. --- stop No parameters. (Regtest only) --- validateaddress Parameter Type Required Description ----------- -------- ---------- ------------------------- address string yes Transparent address --- verifymessage Parameter Type Required Description ------------ -------- ---------- ------------------------- address string yes Transparent address signature string yes Base64 signature message string yes Original message --- walletlock No parameters. --- walletpassphrase Parameter Type Required Description ------------- -------- ---------- -------------------------------------- passphrase string yes Wallet passphrase timeout number yes Seconds to keep the wallet unlocked --- zconverttex Parameter Type Required Description ----------------------- -------- ---------- ---------------------------- transparentaddress string yes P2PKH address to convert --- zexportkey Parameter Type Required Description ----------- -------- ---------- -------------------------------------------------- address string yes Sapling address whose spending key to export Wallet must be unlocked. Only exports the Sapling spending key. --- zgetaccount Parameter T

title: Zcash Mining Guide: Joining a Mining Pool with Personal Hardware
description: Point your GPU or ASIC at a pool, share the work with other miners, and get steady ZEC payouts instead of waiting years for a solo block.
text: Zcash Mining Guide: Joining a Mining Pool with Personal Hardware Point your GPU or ASIC at a pool, share the work with other miners, and get steady ZEC payouts instead of waiting years for a solo block. TL;DR Zcash uses Equihash proof of work. ASICs dominate the network, so GPUs are mainly for hobbyists and testing. Solo mining rarely finds a block for small setups. A pool combines hashrate and pays you a share of each block it finds. You need three things: a Zcash wallet address for payouts, mining hardware, and mining software (or the ASIC's built-in dashboard). Pools differ by fee (about 0-2%), payout method (PPLNS, PPS+), minimum payout and server location. Check profitability first: electricity price, hardware cost and the ZEC price decide whether mining pays at all. Advanced route: run your own Zebra node and mine against its getblocktemplate RPC. Core Explanation Mining is how new Zcash blocks get made. Miners race to solve an Equihash puzzle; the first valid solution adds the next block and earns the block reward. The more hashrate you contribute, the more often you win, but against today's network a single home rig would almost never win on its own. A mining pool fixes that. The pool hands each miner smaller pieces of work called shares. Every accepted share proves you contributed hashrate. When anyone in the pool finds a block, the reward is split according to shares, and you get paid automatically once your balance passes the pool's minimum. The setup has five parts, covered step by step below: A wallet address to receive payouts. Hardware: GPUs in a PC, or an Equihash ASIC. A pool account (or just your address, for pools without registration). Mining software pointed at the pool's stratum server, with YOURADDRESS.WORKERNAME as the user name. Monitoring: accepted shares, hashrate, temperature and unpaid balance. Introduction Zcash (ZEC) is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency that uses the Equihash proof-of-work algorithm for mining. Mining Zcash involves using computational power to solve complex mathematical problems, validating transactions, and securing the network in exchange for ZEC rewards. Due to the network's high difficulty, solo mining is not recommended for most users. Joining a mining pool is the best way to earn consistent rewards by combining your hash power with others. This guide focuses on mining Zcash using personal hardware (e.g., a home PC with GPUs or entry-level ASICs). Note that while GPUs can still mine Zcash, ASICs are far more efficient and profitable in 2026 due to network difficulty. Always check current profitability using tools like WhatToMine.com, as factors like electricity costs, hardware prices, and ZEC value affect viability. Mining may not be profitable for everyone; research local regulations and energy rates (aim for < $0.08/kWh). Requirements Hardware GPU Mining (Personal Setup Recommended for Beginners): NVIDIA or AMD GPUs with at least 4GB VRAM (e.g., NVIDIA GTX 1070, RTX 3060; AMD RX 580 or better). A compatible motherboard, sufficient PSU (at least 750W for multiple GPUs), and good cooling to prevent overheating. Multi-GPU rigs are common for better hash rates (e.g., 6x GPUs can achieve 1-2 kSol/s). ASIC Mining (More Efficient but Higher Cost): Equihash-compatible ASICs like Bitmain Antminer Z15 (420 kSol/s) or Innosilicon A9 (50 kSol/s). These are louder, hotter, and consume more power (e.g., 1500W+); suitable for dedicated spaces. Buy from reputable sources like Bitmain.com or resellers (Blockware Mining). General: Stable internet, a computer for setup/monitoring. ASICs dominate the network (13 GSol/s total hashrate in 2026), making GPU mining less competitive but still possible for hobbyists. Software Operating System: Windows 10/11, Linux (Ubuntu recommended for stability). Mining Software: For GPUs: lolMiner (supports AMD/NVIDIA), GMiner, or miniZ (NVIDIA-focused). Download from official GitHub repos (e.g., github.com/Lolliedieb/lolMiner-releases). For ASICs: Use the manu

title: ZecMap
description: ZecMap is a global, community-driven directory for discovering businesses and services that accept Zcash (ZEC). Built around an interactive map interface, it…
text: ZecMap ZecMap is a global, community-driven directory for discovering businesses and services that accept Zcash (ZEC). Built around an interactive map interface, it helps ZEC holders answer a practical question: "Where can I spend my ZEC?" Website: zecmap.com --- TL;DR ZecMap is a free, public directory of merchants that accept ZEC — local businesses and online shops. Browse the interactive map to find ZEC-friendly merchants near you or anywhere in the world. Anyone can submit a business; listings go through a community review before appearing publicly. A Contributor Rewards Program incentivizes adding and verifying merchant data. ZecMap recently partnered with CipherPay to expand merchant integrations. --- What ZecMap Does ZecMap organizes Zcash-accepting businesses on a global map. Each listing shows the business name, category, location or website, and how ZEC is accepted. This makes it easy for ZEC holders to: Find a nearby cafe, restaurant, hotel, shop, or service that accepts ZEC before making a trip. Discover online stores, VPN providers, freelancers, or digital services that support Zcash payments. Browse regional Zcash adoption by city, country, or travel route. Help keep the directory current as new businesses begin accepting ZEC. --- Use Cases Finding Local Merchants Open zecmap.com and search the map for merchants near you. Before visiting, confirm with the business that ZEC is currently accepted and ask which wallet or payment flow they prefer. Discovering Online Shops and Services ZecMap lists online businesses too. Browse by category to find e-commerce stores, hosting services, VPN providers, and other digital merchants that accept ZEC payments. Planning Travel Around ZEC Traveling to a new city or country? ZecMap lets you browse merchant coverage before you arrive, so you can plan stops at ZEC-friendly restaurants, shops, and services. Supporting New Zcash Users New users often learn how to buy and store ZEC before they discover where to spend it. ZecMap provides that next step — a practical, browsable list of real-world ZEC utility. --- Adding a Business If a business accepts ZEC and is not yet on ZecMap, any community member can submit it. A good submission includes: Field What to provide ------- ---------------- Business name Official name as it appears publicly Website or contact URL or social profile Location Address for physical businesses; region for online Category Cafe, restaurant, store, service, online shop, etc. Evidence Public payments page, merchant announcement, or direct confirmation Payment notes In-person, online, or both; transparent or shielded ZEC Submissions should avoid private customer data. If using transaction proof, remove personal details, order numbers, and home addresses before sharing. --- Verification and Approval Listings go through a review process before appearing publicly: Contributor submits a business with enough public information to verify. The listing is checked for duplicates and basic accuracy. ZEC acceptance is confirmed through a public source or merchant contact. Approved listings appear on the map. Community members can flag stale or incorrect listings so the directory stays current. Because merchant payment options can change, treat listings as community-maintained information, not a guarantee. Confirm with the merchant before a trip or large purchase. --- Contributor Rewards Program ZecMap rewards contributors who help grow and maintain the directory. Rewards are designed to encourage: New listings — adding businesses that accept ZEC and aren't yet on the map. Verification — confirming that existing listings are still active and accurate. Maintenance — updating stale information or flagging closed businesses. Coverage expansion — adding merchants in underrepresented cities, regions, or online categories. For current reward rules and how to claim, visit zecmap.com or check the ZecMap announcements in the Zcash community channels. --- Key Features Interactive globa
